correctness.rationale: The classical row recurrence gives R_s=1−c_s+c_s q_s^s. Write ε=1/s, p=δ_s−γ_s, g=γ_s. Then p+g=ε/c_s and p−g=1/c_s−1. On a fixed bounded complex z-domain, log(1+pz)−log(1−gz) starts at εz; its ε³ coefficient is z/2−z²/4+z³/12, by the linear, quadratic and cubic logarithmic terms. It is odd in ε, with uniform remainder O(ε⁵) by analyticity near ε=0; division by ε and exponentiation give an even R_s expansion through ε². Evaluating at iω−ηε² gives the stated squared-modulus coefficient F(ω)−2η and uniform O(ε⁴). Strict |sin u|<|u| for u≠0 proves the positive defect. On a fixed small real λ interval, the analytic estimates also give convergence of the λ derivative of the squared modulus to 2e^(2λ) by Cauchy estimates. The crossing is unique there for sufficiently large s; the residual at λ=−F/(2s²) is O(s⁻⁴), hence so is the root error. At ω=0 the root is exactly 0. Multiplying the logarithmic squared modulus by floor(Ts²) proves the claimed energy limit. The source's SSP optimality premise is correct for the displayed family, with tableau uniqueness understood up to stage permutations.
residual_risks: Uniformity is only on fixed compact (ω,η) sets. The sign at exactly η=F(ω)/2 is not determined by the leading term. No growing-frequency, nonnormal or nonlinear stability claim is established.

value.rationale: SSP optimality is not a modal energy guarantee. The defect establishes a concrete cost for a standard optimal family: even fixed undamped nonzero frequencies amplify, and a specific weak damping threshold is needed to offset the artificial energy drift. The first nonzero, frequency-dependent defect matters because its effect is order one after O(s²) steps. This differs from both finite-stage plotting and stiff scalar real-axis decay and gives a quantitative, testable calibration for the intended modal regime.
residual_risks: No assertion about practical nonlinear performance, nonnormal systems or implementation costs.
